title: Hot-route capacity protection — Weekly notes (SRE working doc)
content:
Doc purpose
- This is the SRE working doc for the Hot-route capacity protection initiative.
- We use it for: weekly updates, open questions, risk log, decision backlog, and links.
- Audience: SRE + Platform Control Plane + Smart Routing + Runtime + Product + Support readiness.

Last updated: 2025-02-21 (Sean)

Quick status (as of 2025-02-21)
- Core components are converging:
  - Gateway rate limiting middleware is in review/landing (PR 18421) + standardized 429 payload (PR 18463).
  - Router enterprise lane is implemented (PR 18436) + backpressure ingestion (PR 18457).
  - Policy engine schema/validation landed (PR 18444) + rollout/kill-switch (PR 18471).
  - Dashboards and initial alerts are up behind a folder + routing to #eng-oncall (observability-pack PR 922).
  - Perf canary scenarios exist for burst + retry storm (perf-canary PR 311).
- Main risks: config propagation delay + metric cardinality + “fail-open vs fail-closed” behavior under config fetch failures.
- Next SRE deliverables: finalize paging thresholds, validate SLO burn-rate alerts (slo-toolkit PR 188), and publish the on-call runbook + comms checklist.

Owners / contact
- SRE sponsor: Sean Gallagher
- SRE rollout owner: Rafael Mendes
- SLO/dashboards: Aisha Bello (SLOs) + Sergio Costa (dashboards/alerts)
- Control plane: Ethan Park + Jordan Lee (policy engine)
- Routing: Mina Haddad + Elena Popov
- Gateway: Amara Diallo
- Quotas/billing hooks: Cole Summers
- Runtime backpressure: Sofia Ivanova
- Product semantics: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted) + Lauren Bishop (Enterprise/Dedicated)
- Support readiness: Dev Patel

Working definitions (for notes consistency)
- “Hot route”: a single API route/model combo (often enterprise endpoints) that can saturate a region/fleet via traffic surges, retry storms, or pathological prompts.
- “Tier”: enterprise vs self-serve (and internal) lanes for admission/routing.
- “Capacity protection”: combined controls (rate limits, quotas, priority routing/enterprise lanes, and degradation behavior).

================================================================================
Weekly updates
================================================================================

Week of 2025-02-17
Highlights
- Alert tuning proposal drafted; aim is to avoid paging during planned load tests but page on unexpected throttling spikes correlated with elevated queue depth / p99.
- Observability review follow-up: reduced label cardinality plan for throttling metrics; agreed to remove raw customer_id from default metrics (keep in logs/traces only).
- Support reported first real customer confusion: some clients treat 429 as fatal and do not retry; we need docs and SDK snippets ready before broad rollout.

What shipped / merged
- incident-bot PR 77: incident channel summaries for lane health + throttling spikes (pending deploy schedule).

In progress
- slo-toolkit PR 188: per-route/per-tier SLO definitions + burn-rate alerts (Aisha reviewing).
- redwood PR 18471: feature flag + staged rollout by region; verifying rollback is safe under partial config propagation.

Notes / metrics
- During the 2/19 synthetic burst test (internal), enterprise lane remained under p95 target; self-serve throttled earlier than expected (which is okay), but error semantics were inconsistent (some 503s from router when queue overflowed rather than 429 from gateway).
  - Action: tighten “where” we shed (prefer gateway 429 when possible; router should emit consistent reason codes).

Action items
- Rafael: propose paging thresholds for throttled_rate by tier + correlate with saturation signals (due 2025-02-24)
- Sergio: update dashboard panels to default to “route_group” not raw route_id (due 2025-02-26)
- Dev + Wei Chen: draft support macro + public docs snippet for 429 + Retry-After (due 2025-02-28)

Links
- Slack: #eng-oncall thread 1737418821 (paging thresholds)
- Google Drive: throttling-metrics-cardinality-review (obs review notes)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Week of 2025-02-10
Highlights
- Policy engine schema draft stabilized; validation + migration plan discussed with Control Plane.
- Runtime team confirmed reliable backpressure signals + sampling guidance:
  - Use queue depth + prefill saturation as primary triggers.
  - GPU util alone is noisy; use as supporting signal.

What shipped / merged
- redwood PR 18444: policy engine schema + validation (merged)
- redwood PR 18457: runtime backpressure signals -> routing admission (merged)

Decisions made
- We will not page on absolute 429 count. We will page on:
  - sustained throttling rate increase in enterprise lane AND
  - SLO burn-rate risk OR elevated queue depth beyond threshold.
  Rationale: avoid paging during customer-expected quota exhaustion or planned tests.

Open issues
- Config fetch failure behavior not fully resolved:
  - Gateway: if config unavailable, do we fail open (no throttling) or fail closed (throttle aggressively)?
  - Router: same question for lane configuration.
  - Current leaning: fail open for self-serve, fail closed (conservative) for enterprise lane reservation? This is inconsistent; we need a single story + documented behavior.

Action items
- Jordan/Ethan: draft explicit “config unavailable” matrix by component (gateway/router) and tier; propose default + overrides (due 2025-02-14; slipped)
- Mina/Elena: ensure router emits reason codes aligned with gateway (ENG-4826) (due 2025-02-21)

Links
- Slack: #eng-runtime thread 1737141189 (signal reliability)
- Linear: ENG-4825 (backpressure ingestion)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Week of 2025-02-03
Highlights
- Router enterprise lane is functional in simulation harness; still need “bounded fairness” to avoid long-term starvation of lower tiers.
- Product alignment: 429 semantics + Retry-After are required; enterprise accounts expect predictability and “why did I get throttled?” explanation.

What shipped / merged
- redwood PR 18436: router enterprise lane + separate queues (merged)

In progress
- redwood PR 18463: standardized throttling response reason codes + Retry-After (in review)
- observability-pack PR 922: dashboards/alerts (in review)

Operational learnings
- From 1/31 regional dip incident review:
  - Enterprise endpoints were impacted primarily by queueing tail latency (p99 blowups) rather than outright errors.
  - We need degradation mode that sheds early vs letting queues grow uncontrolled.

Action items
- Sean/Rafael: runbook skeleton + comms checklist started; incorporate support feedback (due 2025-02-07; partially done)
- Aisha: draft enterprise hot routes SLO proposal (Confluence doc exists; need review meeting) (due 2025-02-06)

Links
- Slack: #product thread 1737329902 (429 expectations)
- Linear: PM-611 (enterprise throttling UX requirements)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Week of 2025-01-27
Highlights
- Gateway per-route rate limiting middleware landed behind feature flag.
- “Fail-open vs fail-closed” debate continues; SRE prefers:
  - Avoid fleet-wide harm (so do not fail open everywhere).
  - Avoid violating enterprise SLOs via accidental over-throttling.
  => We likely need tier-aware defaults + clear kill-switch.

What shipped / merged
- redwood PR 18421: gateway per-route rate limiting middleware + standardized 429 baseline (merged)

In progress
- ENG-4826: standardize throttling response payloads/headers across gateway and router
- ENG-4827: add observability metrics (throttled_count by route/tier + lane utilization)

Notes
- We should treat delayed metering/quota signals as advisory (soft) initially; quota hard enforcement can cause false 429s when telemetry pipelines lag.

Action items
- Cole: document quota enforcement “delayed metering” behavior + propose initial fail-open approach (due 2025-02-03)
- Allison: formalize metric label guidelines to avoid customer_id cardinality explosion (due 2025-02-05)

Links
- Slack: #eng-platform thread 1737059021 (fail-open vs fail-closed)
- Linear: ENG-4822 (gateway rate limiting)
- Linear: ENG-4823 (quota enforcement)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Week of 2025-01-20
Highlights
- Architecture review: weighted fair queueing (WFQ) vs strict priority for enterprise lane.
- General direction is strict priority with bounded starvation protection.

Decisions made (tentative)
- Router scheduling model: strict priority for enterprise lane; lower tiers receive capacity under “bounded fairness” policy.
  - Follow-up: define “bounded” concretely (time-based? token-based? queue depth-based?).

Risks identified
- Tail latency: strict priority can improve enterprise p99 but may cause uncontrolled queueing for self-serve if we don’t shed early.

Action items
- Mina/Ravi: write down fairness model with crisp parameters and “how to tune safely” notes for oncall (due 2025-01-24)

Links
- Slack: #architecture thread 1737234499 (WFQ vs strict priority)
- Confluence ADR: adr-0147-enterprise-priority-routing-model

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Week of 2025-01-13
Kickoff notes
- Program kickoff in #eng-sre (thread 1736942210). Primary incidents motivating this:
  - Burst + retries on a single enterprise route caused regional saturation.
  - Retry storms + queue growth cascaded to other routes (fleet-wide tail latency).
- SRE asks for: clear semantics, explainable errors, dashboards by route/tier, and a runbook that makes it obvious what’s happening during overload.

Initial scope confirmation
- In scope:
  - Gateway enforcement of per-tenant, per-route, per-region rate limits and quotas.
  - Router priority lanes and enterprise capacity reservation.
  - Runtime backpressure signals integrated into admission/shedding.
  - SRE rollout plan + canary + game day.
- Out of scope:
  - Deep per-customer scheduling inside kernels (runtime roadmap).

Action items
- Sean: create initial SLO targets proposal for top enterprise routes (done via Confluence draft)
- Rafael: draft staged rollout plan outline (started)

================================================================================
Open questions (tracked; please date+sign updates)
================================================================================
1) Fail-open vs fail-closed (config unavailable)
- Question: If policy config cannot be fetched (control plane outage, cache corruption, etc), what is the safe behavior?
- Current options:
  A) Fail open: do not throttle / do not enforce lanes.
  B) Fail closed: enforce conservative defaults (may throttle too aggressively).
  C) Hybrid: enterprise lane defaults preserved (protect SLOs) while self-serve is more aggressively shed.
- SRE position (2025-02-21): prefer C with explicit kill-switch + clear observability to detect “running on defaults”.
- Needs: written matrix by component (gateway/router) and explicit oncall steps.

2) Where to shed first: gateway vs router
- We want 429 + Retry-After from gateway when possible.
- But router may need last-resort shedding (queue caps) under sudden saturation.
- Question: How to ensure reason codes are consistent, and prevent router from returning generic 503 for overload in cases where we could have returned a structured 429?

3) Standard reason codes taxonomy
- Required for support + customer predictability.
- Draft codes seen so far:
  - RATE_LIMIT_PER_ROUTE
  - QUOTA_EXCEEDED
  - ENTERPRISE_LANE_RESERVED
  - OVERLOAD_QUEUE_FULL
  - BACKPRESSURE_PREFILL_SATURATED
  - CONFIG_UNAVAILABLE_DEFAULTS
- Question: Which of these are customer-visible vs internal-only?

4) Config propagation SLO
- Support ticket SUP-24133 suggests inconsistent throttling across regions due to propagation lag.
- Question: Do we commit to an internal SLO for policy propagation (e.g., p95 < 60s) and alert on violations?

5) “Top routes” list and change control
- PM-612 to pick initial list.
- Question: who can add/remove a hot route entry, and what review is required?

================================================================================
Risk log (lightweight; update weekly)
================================================================================
R1: Metric cardinality explosion
- Impact: expensive metrics pipeline + dropped series + blind spots during incident.
- Likelihood: medium (easy to add labels like customer_id).
- Mitigation: enforce label allowlist; aggregate by route_group + tier; customer_id only in logs/traces.
- Owner: Allison Grant
- Status: in progress (review notes captured; dashboards being updated)

R2: Over-throttling enterprise traffic due to misconfig / propagation delay
- Impact: enterprise SLO violation + escalations.
- Likelihood: medium.
- Mitigation: staged rollout by region; config validation; canary accounts; kill-switch; alert on “config defaults” usage.
- Owner: Rafael Mendes + Ethan Park
- Status: open

R3: Under-throttling self-serve during overload -> fleet-wide impact
- Impact: cascading failures; p99 regression for all.
- Likelihood: medium-high during burst events.
- Mitigation: ensure router has last-resort caps; early shedding; perf canary retry-storm tests; game day.
- Owner: Mina Haddad + Sean Gallagher
- Status: open

R4: Customer confusion / poor retry behavior on 429
- Impact: customers amplify load (no backoff) or suffer avoidable downtime (no retries).
- Likelihood: high (observed in SUP-24118).
- Mitigation: docs + SDK guidance; support macros; clear Retry-After semantics; proactive comms to top accounts.
- Owner: Dev Patel + Wei Chen
- Status: in progress

R5: Quota enforcement interacts badly with delayed metering
- Impact: false-positive throttles; revenue/support churn.
- Likelihood: medium.
- Mitigation: fail-open when metering is stale; “metering freshness” signal; start with soft enforcement.
- Owner: Cole Summers
- Status: open

================================================================================
Decision backlog (items that need explicit sign-off)
================================================================================
D1) Priority model: strict priority + bounded fairness parameters
- Needed: concrete definition (token budget? time slice?) and recommended defaults.
- Stakeholders: Routing (Mina), SRE (Sean/Rafael), Product (Lauren).
- Target: before broad rollout (Phase 2/3).

D2) Fail-open/closed policy for config outages
- Needed: matrix by component + tier + what headers/reason codes surface.
- Stakeholders: Control Plane (Ethan/Jordan), Gateway (Amara), Routing (Mina), SRE.

D3) Retry-After semantics
- Needed: is Retry-After always present? seconds vs HTTP date? how computed (static per policy vs dynamic from saturation)?
- Stakeholders: Product (Nikhil), Gateway (Amara), Support (Dev).

D4) Default per-route limits for self-serve
- Needed: initial defaults that won’t cause surprise while still protecting fleet.
- Stakeholders: Product (Nikhil), SRE, Billing hooks (Cole).

D5) Customer-visible “why throttled” fields
- Needed: confirm which reason codes are safe to expose and which are internal.
- Stakeholders: Product + Security/Compliance input (not yet looped).

================================================================================
Upcoming milestones (rough; update as we learn)
================================================================================
- 2025-02-24 to 2025-03-01: finish reason-code/429 consistency across gateway+router; land dashboards + burn-rate alerts.
- 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-14: canary rollout by region + internal load test; game day.
- 2025-03-17+: expand to initial “top routes” list + comms to top accounts.

================================================================================
Appendix: Notes from support escalations (condensed)
================================================================================
SUP-24118 (enterprise burst; elevated 429)
- Customer asked: “Are we being throttled because we exceeded our contract or because the system is overloaded?”
- Ask: make response payload explicit + provide recommended client backoff.

SUP-24133 (inconsistent throttling across regions)
- Suspected cause: config propagation delay between policy engine and edge gateways.
- Follow-up: need propagation visibility + possibly a propagation SLI.

SUP-24155 (Dedicated customer requests explicit reserved throughput for a route)
- Product action: clarify contract language vs platform behavior; ensure lane reservation doesn’t get interpreted as “throughput guarantee” unless explicitly contracted.

End of doc
